subject: Cortico POC confirmation, success criteria and exec readout window
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tucker <alex.tucker@cortico.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Cortico POC — quick recap, proposed success criteria and next steps

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have a shared starting point. Please review and confirm owners and timing; I put a first-pass schedule at the bottom.

Recap (from today's discovery):
- Goal: Reduce clinician note time and surface relevant patient alerts using a lightweight assistant integrated into Cortico's EHR workflow.
- Main constraints: must run against de-identified pilot data, latency target <= 250ms median at 32-token responses, and no PHI stored outside your VPC during the trial.

Proposed POC success criteria (please flag changes):
1) Accuracy: end-user acceptance >= 75% on a 5-point helpfulness rubric across a 500-sample test set defined by Cortico.
2) Latency: median generation latency <= 250ms for standard prompts; 95th <= 700ms during typical burst hours.
3) Integration: simple one-click context pull from EHR sidebar and returned structured JSON payload to the clinician UI.
4) Security: relevant SOC2 artifacts provided and a scoped data access plan agreed (no PHI leaves your environment).

Owners (Redwood):
- POC lead / CS: Mina Haddad
- Solution engineering (integration + infra): Aditya Rao

What we need from Cortico to start:
- Confirm the success criteria above (or note edits)
- A contact for the EHR integration owner (API owner and a test sandbox account)
- Access window / availability for 3-week POC (dates below)
- Completed security questionnaire or a named security contact so we can loop in Redwood security for the SOC2 Q&A

Attachments: RINF-Cortico-POC-Plan-20260914.pdf (first-pass timeline + tasks)

Proposed timeline (first-pass):
- Week 0 (kickoff): sign-off on success criteria, exchange sandbox creds, narrow test dataset
- Week 1: model onboarding + integration prototype (context pull + simple response)
- Week 2: evaluation run on 500-sample set + latency tuning
- Week 3: final readout prep (internal), short demo to Cortico execs and go/no-go decision

Please reply with: (A) confirm owners, (B) confirm data access contact, (C) preferred 1-hour exec readout windows on the week of Sep 28 — we want to lock that now.

Thanks —
Mina
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cortico POC — quick recap, proposed success criteria and next steps

Thanks Mina — that recap looks great and faithful to what we discussed. A few quick notes / minor edits to the criteria and a request on security: 

- Accuracy metric: can we change the acceptance threshold to >=70% on the helpfulness rubric for the pilot? That gives us a safer baseline to start executive conversations.
- Latency: agree with median <=250ms; the 95th at 700ms is OK but can we add a note that 95th should be measured during a simulated clinician-surge (we'll provide a usage trace).
- Integration: we require the output JSON to include a provenance token (request_id + model_version) for audit — can Redwood include that in the prototype?

Security / data access: our security lead Samantha Li will own the questionnaire and the SOC2 review. She may ask for an RBAC diagram and data flow. I copied her on this thread.

Owners from Cortico:
- Product-owner / POC sponsor: Alex Tucker (me)
- Integration contact: Samantha Li (samantha.li@cortico.com)

We can commit to the 3-week window, but our dev team prefers a kick on Sep 22 so the readout happens the week of Sep 28 — can you confirm Redwood availability for a Sep 28 exec readout?

Happy to hop on a quick 15-min sync if useful.

Cheers,
Alex
Senior Product Manager — AI, Cortico Therapeutics
alex.tucker@cortico.com

Thanks Alex — confirmed on the changes: we'll set the acceptance threshold to >=70% and add a provenance token (request_id + model_version) in the JSON output. We'll also measure 95th latency using your usage trace.

Updated owners / responsibilities (Redwood):
- Mina Haddad — POC / CS lead (program coordination, acceptance gating)
- Aditya Rao — Solutions Engineering (integration, latency tuning, model variants)
- Redwood Security (contact: security@redwood.com) — to handle SOC2 artifacts and provide the RBAC/data-flow diagram

Attachments included: Cortico_POC_Success_Criteria.xlsx (editable sheet with test set, rubric, and measurement plan) and SOC2-questions-answers-stub.pdf (initial answers to the typical items your security team raises).

Evaluation plan (short):
- Week 1: integration prototype + smoke tests against sanitized sandbox
- Week 2: run evaluation harness over your 500-sample set (we'll both run local and collect metrics in Redwood Console)
- Week 3: joint validation week — collect final metrics, prepare executive-readout slide deck and decision memo

Proposed kickoff: Sep 22, 2026 (Mon) 10:00 AM PT — duration 30-45 minutes. Does that work for your team?

Exec readout: we propose Sep 29 (Tue) 11:00 AM PT or Sep 30 (Wed) 10:00 AM PT as alternates if Sep 28 won't work for Redwood execs. We want to lock a 45-minute slot for a short demo and a go/no-go discussion.

Next contract step: if Cortico decides to proceed after a successful readout we will provide a term sheet and dedicated capacity quote; Marissa (cc'd) will manage the commercial route.

Regards,
Mina
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Mina — looping in to confirm commercial & exec timing. Thanks for the clear alignment on success criteria and owners. A few operational notes from my side: 

1) Exec readout scheduling: Mina proposed Sep 29 / Sep 30 windows — our execs have an opening on Sep 28 at 11:00 AM PT for a 45-minute slot (we can make Sep 29 11:00 as backup). Please confirm whether your exec sponsor can attend Sep 28 11:00. If not, we'll take Sep 29 11:00.

2) Contract path & timeline: assuming a successful go decision at the readout we will:
- Day 0..3 after go: Marissa to send term sheet + pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted options
- Day 3..10: procurement / legal review at Cortico; we can provide a short SOW addendum for the pilot if you prefer a lightweight commercial commit.

3) Commercial ask: to secure reserved integration support during the 3-week POC we typically request a modest refundable POC retainer (details in the term sheet). If procurement prefers not to, we can instead formalize a brief SOW with defined deliverables.

4) Security artifacts: Mina — can you share the RBAC/data-flow diagram by EOD Mon Sep 20 so Samantha has it before the kickoff? Samantha — if Redwood Security should just open a Jira ticket with your team, we can route the SOC2 Q&A there.

Action items summary:
- Alex: confirm exec availability for Sep 28 11:00 PT (or confirm Sep 29 backup) — reply here
- Samantha: confirm preferred mechanism for SOC2 Q&A (Jira/Doc) and any additional info you need before kickoff
- Mina / Aditya: prep integration checklist and initial evaluation harness (deliver to the shared Drive link)
- Marissa: will draft term sheet and POC retainer options to circulate after readout

Alex — if you confirm Sep 28 at 11:00 we'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: 1) 10-min demo, 2) metrics review, 3) go/no-go discussion, 4) next contract steps.

Thanks,
